author: Vitor
notes: Attempt at solving using a sort of backtrack solution, didn't even bother with code quality - a function called `gogo`, very professional.
aiExplanation: This function finds the **smallest permutation** of the letters in `s` that is **lexicographically greater** than `target`. It first counts how many times each letter appears in `s` using a 26-slot `freq` array. The recursive helper `gogo` then builds the answer one character at a time: at each position it first tries to **match** the corresponding character of `target` (if that letter is still available), recursing deeper to see if a valid result can be completed with an identical prefix; if that path fails, it **backtracks** (restores the count) and instead picks the *smallest available letter strictly greater* than the target's character at that position — once a bigger letter is placed, the string is already guaranteed to beat `target`, so the helper `fill` simply appends all remaining letters in **ascending alphabetical order** to keep the result as small as possible. When the recursion consumes as many characters as `target` has, it checks `str > target` to accept or reject the candidate, and an empty string `''` is used throughout to signal "no valid answer down this path".

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This is a cleaner take on the same idea: build the **smallest rearrangement** of `s` that is **lexicographically greater** than `target`, using a letter-count array `freq` shared by all the helpers. The `dfs` function walks through the positions of `target`, and at each position it loops over the available letters starting from the target's own character (`start`): if it can place a **strictly bigger** letter (`i > start`), the result is already guaranteed to win the comparison, so `fill` immediately appends every leftover letter in **sorted ascending order** to finish with the smallest possible tail; if it places the **same** letter as `target`, it must recurse one level deeper (`dfs(pos + 1, ...)`) to decide the tie further along, and if that deeper search comes back empty it **backtracks** by restoring `freq[i]++` and tries the next bigger letter instead. Reaching the end of `target` with a matched prefix triggers the final check `str > target`, and an empty string is returned anywhere a valid answer can't be formed.
